label: corruption_suite_external_validity
shared_hypothesis: Synthetic-corruption robustness benchmarks do not predict robustness to real acquisition degradations; ranking correlation across model families is too weak for corruption suites to work as selection tools.

members.one_line: Synthetic-corruption robustness rankings mispredict real-degradation robustness rankings: the rank correlation across model families is weak enough to invalidate corruption suites as selection tools.
members.note: rank-correlation formulation across model families; most operational version

members.one_line: Synthetic corruption benchmarks do not predict real acquisition-degradation robustness for segmentation.
members.note: fold into w14w2b-116: identical corruption-suites-do-not-predict-real-robustness claim, bare form

members.one_line: Methods ranked on sim-to-real benchmarks do not rank the same on real-to-real shifts because the two shift families have structurally different statistics, making the standard benchmark a biased method selector
members.note: same external-validity failure for sim-to-real vs real-to-real shift benchmarks; different benchmark family

members.one_line: Corruption robustness decomposes by subtask: image corruptions degrade classification while boxes persist (or vice versa per corruption family), so robustness interventions should be subtask-targeted
members.note: adds subtask decomposition: corruptions hit classification vs localization asymmetrically

label: crawl_contamination_of_benchmarks
shared_hypothesis: Standard dense benchmarks overlap web pretraining crawls, so zero-shot/grounding scores are exposure-inflated; post-cutoff imagery exposes the inflation.

members.one_line: Dense benchmarks are inside the pretraining crawl: grounding scores on standard test images are inflated by exposure, measurable with post-cutoff imagery
members.note: post-cutoff-imagery test; grounding formulation

members.one_line: Zero-shot segmentation evaluations of web-pretrained models are contaminated: benchmark imagery overlaps pretraining crawls, and post-crawl imagery exposes the inflation.
members.note: fold into w14E-101: identical crawl-contamination + post-crawl-imagery hypothesis, zero-shot segmentation arm

members.one_line: Restoration and segmentation benchmarks share source imagery, so restoration models can memorize the clean versions of segmentation test images, silently inflating restoration-utility studies.
members.note: shared source imagery lets restoration models memorize clean test images; adjacent leakage channel

members.one_line: Generative augmentation can leak test sets through memorization: models trained on diffusion outputs inherit near-duplicates of the generator's training images, including benchmark test images.
members.note: generative augmentation leaks test sets via generator memorization; different leakage mechanism

members.one_line: Open-vocab benchmarks with static base-novel splits have been community-overfit: years of method development tuned on the same 'novel' classes inflates novel-class AP relative to genuinely fresh splits
members.note: community overfitting to static base-novel splits; human-process contamination, not crawl overlap

label: word_frequency_determines_openvocab
shared_hypothesis: Per-class open-vocab performance is governed by the class name's text-corpus/caption frequency more than by visual difficulty.

members.one_line: Per-class dense performance is a language-statistics artifact: pretraining word frequency out-predicts visual difficulty measures for open-vocab segmentation quality
members.note: frequency out-predicts visual-difficulty measures; dense formulation

members.one_line: Open-vocabulary segmentation is high-resource-vocabulary segmentation: per-class performance tracks caption-word frequency more than visual difficulty.
members.note: fold into w14E-106: identical frequency-beats-visual-difficulty claim, contrarian phrasing

members.one_line: Open-vocab detection AP per category is driven more by the category name's text-corpus frequency than by visual difficulty, and renaming to a frequent synonym changes AP
members.note: detection arm; adds causal renaming-to-frequent-synonym intervention

members.one_line: Similarity-map sharpness tracks word frequency, not visual distinctiveness: rare words get diffuse maps regardless of how salient the object is
members.note: mechanism readout: similarity-map sharpness tracks word frequency

members.one_line: Synonym consistency is the missing invariance metric: open-vocab segmenters give materially different masks for 'couch' and 'sofa'
members.note: synonym-consistency as an invariance metric; measurement proposal on same substrate

label: caption_salience_alignment_cap
shared_hypothesis: Caption-mention statistics (what people bother to name) bound what contrastively/caption-supervised models can ground; rarely-mentioned objects and regions are unfindable regardless of decoder or architecture.

members.one_line: Contrastive pretraining's salience bias caps dense recall: objects that captions rarely mention are unfindable regardless of decoder quality
members.note: salience bias caps dense recall; general form

members.one_line: Caption-supervised detection inherits salience bias: objects that captions mention get detected, background instances of the same class get missed, measurable as a mention-likelihood recall gradient
members.note: detection arm; within-class mention-likelihood recall gradient is a distinct measurable law

members.one_line: The stuff-thing gap in open-vocab segmentation is caption-statistics debt: regions that captions rarely mention cannot be aligned, whatever the architecture
members.note: stuff-thing gap reattributed to caption statistics; distinct benchmark-level prediction

members.one_line: Caption supervision teaches nameability, not segmentability: language-supervised features underperform on visually-coherent but rarely-named regions.
members.note: fold into w14E-107: identical rarely-named-regions-cannot-align claim (nameability vs segmentability)

members.one_line: Pseudo-label bootstrapping amplifies CLIP's salience bias generation over generation: self-trained dense models drift toward segmenting only what captions mention
members.note: generational amplification of salience bias under pseudo-label bootstrapping

members.one_line: Foundation-feature generality fails on stuff classes: frozen VFM features are object-biased and lose to older supervised features on amorphous regions.
members.note: object-biased VFM features fail on stuff; feature-level mechanism, not caption statistics

label: annotation_noise_floor
shared_hypothesis: Below a size/frequency threshold, benchmark metrics measure annotation noise rather than model capability: inter-annotator agreement bounds achievable scores and reorders leaderboards.

members.one_line: Below a size floor, small-object AP measures annotation noise, not detection: inter-annotator box IoU for tiny objects bounds achievable AP and reorders leaderboard conclusions
members.note: small-object AP bounded by inter-annotator box IoU; most operational

members.one_line: Small-object segmentation leaderboards measure annotation noise: below an area threshold, GT boundary placement error exceeds model differences.
members.note: fold into w14D2-047 as segmentation arm: identical below-threshold-GT-noise-exceeds-model-differences claim

members.one_line: Rare-class AP in long-tail detection benchmarks primarily measures annotation agreement, not model capability: label noise on rare classes bounds and scrambles the metric that the field optimizes
members.note: same noise-floor hypothesis on the frequency axis (rare classes) rather than size axis

members.one_line: High-IoU evaluation thresholds measure annotation-style agreement rather than perceived localization quality: beyond the annotator-consistency ceiling, AP@0.9 stops correlating with human preference
members.note: high-IoU thresholds measure annotation style; threshold-axis variant

members.one_line: Ground-truth quality co-varies with image quality: annotations on degraded images are noisier, so measured robustness curves conflate model degradation with reference degradation.
members.note: GT quality co-varies with image degradation, confounding robustness curves

label: leaderboard_statistical_noise
shared_hypothesis: Reported benchmark deltas at the top of leaderboards are within measurement noise (bootstrap variance, GT reproducibility), so parts of the progress narrative are unfalsifiable.

members.one_line: Benchmark mAP differences between adjacent leaderboard entries are often within bootstrap confidence intervals, and the field's progress narrative at the top end is partly statistical noise
members.note: bootstrap CIs on adjacent leaderboard entries

members.one_line: A sizeable share of recent benchmark deltas sit below the ground-truth reproducibility floor, making them unfalsifiable as scientific claims.
members.note: GT-reproducibility floor version; different noise source, same unfalsifiability claim

members.one_line: Most published fairness-accuracy tradeoff points for dense models are statistically indistinguishable: the tradeoff is underpowered, not established.
members.note: fairness-accuracy tradeoff points statistically indistinguishable; same power critique in fairness

label: spatial_error_correlation_breaks_iid
shared_hypothesis: Dense-prediction errors are spatially correlated, violating the i.i.d. assumptions of classification-derived statistics (variance estimates, transferability estimators, DG bounds).

members.one_line: Tile-level i.i.d. aggregation in WSI and large-image benchmarks understates variance because errors cluster spatially, making many published significance claims unsupported.
members.note: tile-level i.i.d. aggregation understates variance; significance claims unsupported

members.one_line: Classification-derived transferability estimators fail for segmentation because spatial error correlation violates their independence assumptions, and their failure is predictable from error-cluster size
members.note: same violation breaks transferability estimators; error-cluster-size predictor

members.one_line: Dense prediction breaks classification-derived domain-generalization theory because errors propagate spatially: one shifted region corrupts its neighborhood through receptive fields, violating i.i.d.-example bounds
members.note: theory form: spatial propagation breaks classification DG bounds

label: bagofwords_compositional_blindness
shared_hypothesis: Open-vocab/VL dense models process queries as bags of words: relations, modifiers, and attribute bindings are largely ignored, measurable by swap/compliance tests.

members.one_line: Vision-language detectors inherit bag-of-words relational blindness: spatial-relation queries retrieve the right objects with near-chance relational correctness, quantifiable as a relation-compliance metric
members.note: relation-swap near-chance compliance; quantified relation-compliance metric

members.one_line: Referring-expression segmentation models ignore relational language: swapping spatial relations changes few predictions.
members.note: fold into w14D2-082: identical relational-blindness relation-swap claim, referring-segmentation arm

members.one_line: Open-vocab detectors detect the head noun and largely ignore compositional modifiers, so 'red valve wheel' style queries silently degrade to 'wheel' with a measurable modifier-compliance rate
members.note: modifier-compliance version: queries degrade to head noun; distinct compliance metric

members.one_line: Attribute binding fails silently in dense grounding: 'the red cup next to the blue cup' picks a cup by salience because attributes are pooled bag-of-words style
members.note: attribute-binding failure by salience; dense grounding arm

members.one_line: Compositional queries degrade multiplicatively: each added attribute multiplies error odds, revealing independent per-constraint filtering with no joint parsing
members.note: multiplicative per-constraint error law; distinct quantitative prediction

members.one_line: Attribute words in open-vocab queries relocate boxes toward the attribute-bearing subregion instead of gating detection, producing systematically distorted boxes for attribute queries
members.note: attribute words relocate boxes instead of gating; geometric side effect

members.one_line: Evidence hierarchy under conflict: when the attribute contradicts the image ('the wooden dog'), the noun wins and the conflict leaves no trace in output confidence
members.note: noun-wins evidence hierarchy under image-text conflict

label: query_list_interference
shared_hypothesis: Detections/masks for a class depend on which other classes are in the query list: score renormalization couples nominally independent queries.

members.one_line: Multi-class text queries interact inside grounding detectors: a class's AP depends on which other classes are queried alongside it, violating the independence assumption of every deployment
members.note: independence violation stated and tested directly

members.one_line: Open-vocab detectors pay a vocabulary-size tax: AP on a fixed class degrades as unrelated query classes are added, quantifying an unreported interference effect
members.note: fold into w14D2-081: same vocabulary-size-tax measurement of the same interference effect

members.one_line: Vocabulary interference: adding irrelevant classes to the query list changes detections of unrelated classes through score renormalization
members.note: adds the mechanism (score renormalization); dense arm

members.one_line: Large query vocabularies self-poison: false-positive rates per query grow with the semantic density of the vocabulary, not just its size
members.note: FP growth law in semantic density, not just list length

members.one_line: Hierarchical vocabularies break open-vocab detectors: querying 'animal' and 'dog' together splits scores and drops both below threshold
members.note: hierarchical special case: hypernym+hyponym queries split scores

members.one_line: Synonyms sail through class-aware NMS: querying near-duplicate vocabulary items produces duplicate boxes that standard suppression logic cannot merge
members.note: synonym queries evade class-aware NMS; duplicate-box consequence

members.one_line: Negative vocabulary is the underused half of open-vocab detection: adding confusable distractor class names cuts false positives more than any tuning of the positive prompt
members.note: TENSION: negative/confusable vocabulary items HELP (cut FPs) vs E-034 self-poisoning

label: part_whole_query_default
shared_hypothesis: Part-level queries return whole objects because region-text alignment is object-centric; part-whole structure is systematically mishandled.

members.one_line: Part queries default to the whole: 'the handle of the cup' returns the cup whenever the part boundary is not photometrically obvious
members.note: photometric-boundary moderator gives sharpest falsifiable condition

members.one_line: Querying part names in open-vocab detectors returns whole objects at a high rate because region-text alignment was trained object-centric, defining a measurable part-query failure mode
members.note: fold into w14E-110 as detection arm: identical part-query-returns-whole claim with object-centric-alignment mechanism

members.one_line: Part-whole boundaries are training-unstable: pixels belonging to both 'person' and 'shirt' receive conflicting gradients, leaving a detectable noise signature along part seams
members.note: conflicting gradients at part seams leave detectable noise signature; training-dynamics mechanism

members.one_line: Many surviving duplicate detections are not noise but part-whole ambiguity, and suppressing them destroys recoverable hierarchical structure
members.note: NMS-surviving duplicates are recoverable part-whole structure

members.one_line: Occlusion language is evaluated incoherently: 'the partially hidden cat' has amodal semantics but modal ground truth, and models are punished whichever they output
members.note: amodal-vs-modal evaluation incoherence for occlusion language

members.one_line: Language can probe amodal knowledge without amodal training: asking for 'the whole object including hidden parts' recovers completion that binary evaluation says models lack
members.note: language probes latent amodal knowledge without amodal training

label: openvocab_nearest_neighbor_retrieval
shared_hypothesis: Open-vocabulary recognition is interpolation/nearest-neighbor retrieval around seen classes: novel or rare words inherit the behavior and shapes of their closest seen neighbors.

members.one_line: Open vocabulary is nearest-neighbor retrieval in disguise: novel-word masks inherit the shape statistics of the closest seen class
members.note: shape-statistics inheritance formulation

members.one_line: Rare-word queries return the frequent cousin: 'ocelot' produces cat-shaped masks because open vocabulary regresses to taxonomic neighbors
members.note: fold into w14E-063: 'ocelot yields cat-shaped masks' is the same neighbor-regression claim, rare-word arm

members.one_line: Open-vocab detection performance is interpolation in embedding space: accuracy on 'novel' classes is predicted by their distance to seen classes, exposing how little is actually open
members.note: quantitative law: novel-class accuracy predicted by embedding distance to seen classes

members.one_line: Open-vocab errors on rare classes are systematically superclass substitutions, because rare-class text embeddings collapse toward their frequent hypernyms
members.note: detection arm with hypernym-collapse mechanism for rare classes

members.one_line: Zero-shot-on-novel-classes claims are synonym leakage: truly novel coined categories drop open-vocab models to near chance.
members.note: synonym-leakage audit with coined-category probe; strongest falsification design in cluster

label: plurality_quantifier_grouping
shared_hypothesis: Grammatical number and quantifiers steer instance grouping: plural/exhaustive queries under-return or merge instances because referring-style supervision taught one-answer-per-query.

members.one_line: Grammatical number in open-vocab queries steers instance grouping: plural queries bias toward group boxes and merged detections, singular toward instance boxes
members.note: singular/plural grouping contrast in detection

members.one_line: Plural queries collapse instances into blobs: 'the dogs' returns one connected mask whose topology depends on instance spacing, not on countability
members.note: mask-topology-vs-spacing law; distinct measurable prediction

members.one_line: Grounding-data-trained detectors carry a single-referent bias: they under-return exhaustive instances because referring expressions taught one-answer-per-query, measurable as an instance-count saturation curve
members.note: single-referent bias with instance-count saturation curve; same training-data mechanism

members.one_line: Universal quantifiers are dropped: 'every dog' and 'the dog' produce the same single-instance mask because referring data taught one-expression-one-object
members.note: universal quantifiers dropped; same one-expression-one-object mechanism, quantifier probe

label: hallucination_placement_priors
shared_hypothesis: Hallucinated detections/masks/fabrications are not random: they land at contextually plausible locations predictable from co-occurrence, position priors, or embedding proximity.

members.one_line: Hallucinated masks are scene-conditional: absent-but-plausible objects get grounded at high rates while absent-and-implausible ones do not
members.note: scene-plausibility law for absent-object grounding

members.one_line: Open-set detectors produce confident boxes for absent queried classes at rates predictable from embedding proximity to present objects, defining a measurable and correctable query-hallucination law
members.note: embedding-proximity law for absent queried classes; distinct predictor, same phenomenon

members.one_line: Hallucinated masks are placed at dataset position priors: querying an absent object yields a mask where that object usually appears in training data
members.note: dataset position priors determine hallucinated mask placement

members.one_line: Detector false positives are context-conditioned hallucinations: the FP class distribution in a scene matches co-occurrence statistics of the training set, enabling context-debiased rescoring
members.note: FP class distribution matches training co-occurrence; enables context-debiased rescoring

members.one_line: Generative restoration fabricates objects preferentially at contextually plausible locations, so hallucination-induced false positives evade anomaly-based quality control.
members.note: generative restoration fabricates at plausible locations, evading anomaly QC; restoration arm

members.one_line: High-confidence background hallucinations have a distinct logit signature (anomalous margin structure) that separates them from true detections without retraining
members.note: logit-signature detector for hallucinated detections; countermeasure claim

label: negation_absence_blindness
shared_hypothesis: Negation and absence are structurally missing from caption-supervised dense models: negated terms attract, 'without' is invisible, abstention is unavailable, and scale does not fix it.

members.one_line: 'Without' is invisible: dense models ground 'person without a hat' onto hatted people at near-baseline rates
members.note: 'without' grounded onto the negated attribute at near-baseline rates

members.one_line: Negated attributes attract: 'the cup that is not red' selects the red cup more often than chance, inverting the query's meaning
members.note: negated attributes actively attract (worse than chance); inversion form of the same blindness

members.one_line: Negation in language-guided segmentation does not improve with scale: absence semantics is structurally missing from caption supervision at every size.
members.note: scale-invariance claim: absence semantics missing at every model size

members.one_line: Grounding models cannot say 'not present': under empty-target queries they emit confident masks, and no benchmark penalizes it
members.note: no not-present output channel; benchmark-design consequence

members.one_line: 'Present but small' and 'absent' are inseparable in open-vocab score space, making abstention on small objects fundamentally unreliable
members.note: small-vs-absent inseparability in score space; abstention impossibility result

label: vae_latent_resolution_floor
shared_hypothesis: Latent-space autoencoders impose a hard minimum resolvable structure size (the downsampling factor), creating a thin-structure floor for anything routed through latents.

members.one_line: Latent-space autoencoders in latent diffusion impose a hard minimum resolvable structure size, creating a resolution floor no decoder fine-tuning can cross for segmentation through latents.
members.note: direct statement of the latent resolution floor for segmentation through latents

members.one_line: Latent-space mask conditioning destroys thin structures below the autoencoder's downsampling factor, so latent-diffusion synthetic data systematically hurts thin-structure classes
members.note: same floor expressed through latent-diffusion synthetic data harming thin-structure classes; distinct downstream readout

label: structured_degradation_realism
shared_hypothesis: Real degradations are spatially/semantically structured (coupled to depth, motion, semantics); training with uniform synthetic degradation teaches physically wrong invariances.

members.one_line: Real-world degradations are correlated with semantics (blur on movers, defocus on background), so training with spatially uniform synthetic degradation teaches wrong invariances and can reduce real-world robustness.
members.note: semantics-correlated degradation; wrong-invariance claim

members.one_line: Turbidity acts as a range-dependent low-pass filter, so underwater augmentation must couple blur strength to scene depth; uniform-blur augmentation teaches physically impossible images and transfers worse
members.note: underwater instance: turbidity blur must couple to depth; same uniform-augmentation-is-wrong mechanism

members.one_line: Defocus and depth-of-field statistics are a first-order sim-to-real axis for close-range robotic segmentation, unlike for driving where they are negligible
members.note: defocus/DoF as first-order axis for close-range only; domain-dependence claim

label: camera_isp_shift
shared_hypothesis: The camera ISP/processing pipeline is a dominant, reproducible axis of domain shift that content-level realism work and photometric augmentation do not address.

members.one_line: The camera ISP is a hidden confounder in segmentation datasets: much of what is called cross-camera domain shift is reproducible ISP shift.
members.note: cross-camera shift decomposed as reproducible ISP shift

members.one_line: Simulating the camera pipeline (demosaicing, noise model, tone curve) closes a larger share of the sim-to-real gap than improving content realism, for matched effort
members.note: sim-to-real arm: simulating the ISP closes more gap than content realism at matched effort

members.one_line: Strong photometric augmentation narrows models to the benchmark camera pipeline instead of broadening them: on truly novel pipelines it backfires.
members.note: TENSION-adjacent: strong photometric augmentation narrows models to the benchmark pipeline

members.one_line: Sensor fixed-pattern noise acts as a device watermark that segmentation models learn, coupling predictions to the capture device rather than the scene.
members.note: fixed-pattern sensor noise as learned device watermark; device-coupling consequence

label: jpeg_block_grid_prior
shared_hypothesis: Models trained on compressed data learn the codec's block grid and artifact structure as spatial priors, with measurable grid-aligned output biases.

members.one_line: Segmentation models trained on JPEG-compressed data learn the 8x8 block grid as a boundary prior, measurably snapping mask edges to block boundaries.
members.note: mask edges snap to 8x8 block boundaries

members.one_line: Compression artifacts create block-aligned phantom detections: small-object false positives cluster on 8-pixel JPEG grid boundaries, and grid-aware filtering removes them without touching true positives
members.note: detection arm: block-aligned phantom FPs plus grid-aware filtering fix

members.one_line: Video segmentation models trained on compressed footage exploit codec artifacts as motion cues, so they degrade on raw or differently encoded video: a reverse domain gap.
members.note: codec artifacts exploited as motion cues; reverse domain gap on raw video

members.one_line: Video segmentation accuracy oscillates with codec GOP structure: masks are measurably better on I-frames than on B-frames, creating a periodic artifact no shuffled-frame evaluation can see.
members.note: GOP-periodic accuracy oscillation invisible to shuffled-frame evaluation

label: generated_image_contamination
shared_hypothesis: 'Real' web-scraped datasets already contain generated/AI-processed imagery, and this contamination measurably distorts training and evaluation conclusions.

members.one_line: Web-scraped segmentation datasets assembled after 2022 already contain diffusion-generated images, and this contamination measurably distorts benchmark conclusions.
members.note: post-2022 diffusion-image contamination with benchmark-distortion measurement

members.one_line: Public 'real' benchmarks are drifting synthetic-ward as web-scraped generated imagery leaks in, silently flattering synthetic-trained models in evaluation
members.note: fold into w14w2b-077: same benchmarks-drifting-synthetic-ward claim; keep its synthetic-trained-model-flattering readout as an arm

members.one_line: The real-image supply is drifting: web photographs are increasingly SR-processed and AI-enhanced before upload, so datasets of the future inherit restoration priors in their supposedly natural images.
members.note: SR/AI-enhancement of uploads puts restoration priors into 'natural' images; processing not generation

members.one_line: Segmentation models are systematically more accurate on generated images than on real ones at matched apparent difficulty, making the accuracy gap itself a contamination detector.
members.note: accuracy gap on generated vs real images as a contamination detector; diagnostic application

members.one_line: Invisible watermarks embedded in synthetic training images become learned features, coupling segmentation models to watermark schemes that will change under them.
members.note: invisible watermarks become learned features; scheme-coupling harm

label: self_consuming_loop_collapse
shared_hypothesis: Self-consuming generate-train loops degrade boundary complexity first, and boundary-entropy decline is a quantitative early-warning signal of collapse.

members.one_line: Self-consuming training loops for segmentation collapse boundary complexity before class statistics shift, providing an early-warning metric generations before visible model collapse.
members.note: boundary complexity collapses generations before visible model collapse

members.one_line: Iterative self-generation loops (model labels real images, generator trains on them, model retrains on generated pairs) collapse at a rate predictable from boundary-entropy loss per cycle
members.note: fold into w14w2b-079: same boundary-entropy-per-cycle collapse law stated as a rate prediction

label: distillation_bias_inheritance
shared_hypothesis: Distillation and pseudo-label supervision transfer the teacher's systematic error structure to students: biases are inherited, not averaged out, capping quality and destroying error diversity.

members.one_line: Distillation transfers the teacher's failure map more than its skill: distilled students are accuracy-similar but error-correlated, destroying ensemble and audit value.
members.note: general error-correlation form; ensemble/audit-value destruction is the sharpest consequence

members.one_line: Distillation from synthetic-trained teachers transfers their domain biases to students trained on real data, so 'clean' student pipelines silently inherit synthetic artifacts one generation removed
members.note: synthetic-domain biases inherited one generation removed; provenance-specific arm

members.one_line: Foundation-model masks as free supervision cap student quality below human-label training: teacher biases are inherited, not averaged out.
members.note: foundation-model pseudo-labels cap students below human-label training; quality-ceiling arm

members.one_line: Distilling per-frame pseudo-labels into video models amplifies flicker-consistent errors: mistakes that happen to be temporally stable get promoted to confident learned structure.
members.note: video arm: temporally stable teacher errors get promoted to confident structure

members.one_line: Self-distillation gains on segmentation are repackaged schedule and augmentation extensions, not knowledge transfer.
members.note: self-distillation gains reattributed to schedule/augmentation; nonreplication angle

members.one_line: Retraining on human-corrected model outputs plateaus early: correction data inherits the model's boundary style and cannot teach past it.
members.note: human-corrected model outputs inherit the model's boundary style; correction-loop ceiling

label: synthetic_occlusion_gap
shared_hypothesis: Synthetic scenes systematically under-occlude relative to reality, and occlusion-statistics mismatch predicts sim-to-real failure better than image-realism metrics.

members.one_line: Synthetic scenes systematically under-occlude, and occlusion-statistics mismatch predicts sim-to-real transfer failure better than image-level realism metrics
members.note: occlusion-statistics mismatch as transfer predictor

members.one_line: Synthetic scenes have systematically simpler occlusion topology than reality, and occlusion complexity is the variable that predicts where synthetically pretrained segmenters fail on real data.
members.note: fold into w14w2a-024: identical simpler-occlusion-topology-predicts-failure claim

members.one_line: Layout realism (object co-occurrence and spatial arrangement statistics) explains more sim-to-real gap than per-object appearance realism for scene segmentation
members.note: layout realism (co-occurrence/arrangement) beats appearance realism; broader scene-statistics claim

members.one_line: After style transfer 'closes' the appearance gap, the residual sim-to-real gap is mostly boundary micro-geometry, measurable by boundary curvature spectra of the two domains
members.note: residual gap after style transfer is boundary micro-geometry; complementary decomposition

label: temporal_consistency_tradeoff
shared_hypothesis: Temporal-consistency objectives buy smoothness by paying accuracy along an unmeasured Pareto frontier, and standard reporting hides the exchange rate; much flicker is fixable post hoc for free.

members.one_line: Temporal-consistency losses trade single-frame accuracy for stability along an unmeasured Pareto frontier: the exchange rate varies by class and is often worse than post-hoc smoothing achieves for free
members.note: explicit Pareto framing with post-hoc-smoothing comparator

members.one_line: Temporal-consistency losses buy smoothness, not accuracy: they trade boundary fidelity for reduced flicker and the trade is hidden by reporting choices.
members.note: fold into w14D2-118: identical consistency-loss-trades-accuracy-for-smoothness claim, segmentation arm

members.one_line: Video detection flicker is mostly threshold-crossing of smoothly varying scores, not representational instability: hysteresis thresholding eliminates the majority of flicker at negligible accuracy cost
members.note: flicker is threshold-crossing; hysteresis fix at negligible cost

members.one_line: Frame-wise video detection metrics hide temporal flicker: models with equal per-frame mAP differ hugely in detection persistence, and a flicker-penalizing metric would reorder method preference for video deployments
members.note: frame-wise metrics blind to persistence; metric proposal

members.one_line: Video super-resolution creates mask flicker: per-frame quality improves while temporal instability of downstream segmentation exceeds that of the degraded input.
members.note: video SR improves frames while destabilizing downstream masks; restoration-induced flicker

members.one_line: Temporal-quality metrics for video restoration do not predict downstream tracking and segmentation stability: the two notions of temporal consistency are measurably different constructs.
members.note: temporal-quality metrics don't predict downstream stability; construct-validity claim

members.one_line: Sparse annotation cadence in video benchmarks rewards persistence-biased models: dense re-annotation of even short spans flips method rankings toward event-responsive models.
members.note: sparse annotation cadence rewards persistence-biased models; benchmark-design confound

label: video_memory_value
shared_hypothesis: Long temporal memory in video segmentation does not buy accuracy: information saturates within a few frames and long memory adds drift, so cheap per-frame ensembling competes with dedicated temporal machinery.

members.one_line: Memory-based video object segmentation anti-scales with memory length on long videos: more stored frames means more drift, not more accuracy.
members.note: anti-scaling (drift) form; TENSION with w14w2b-104 saturation form

members.one_line: Temporal information for streaming segmentation saturates within a few frames: long-memory architectures buy identity persistence, not segmentation accuracy, and the two are conflated in benchmarks.
members.note: saturation form: long memory buys identity persistence, not accuracy; benchmark conflation claim

members.one_line: Streaming memory segmenters amplify temporally correlated restoration errors: preprocessing that helps per-frame models destabilizes memory-based ones superlinearly.
members.note: memory amplifies temporally correlated input errors superlinearly

members.one_line: Dedicated video architectures lose to temporally-ensembled per-frame models at matched compute on stable-camera domains.
members.note: temporally-ensembled per-frame models beat video architectures at matched compute

members.one_line: Optical-flow label propagation now produces worse training signal than per-frame pseudo-labeling: modern model quality has crossed the flow-error floor.
members.note: flow-based label propagation now worse than per-frame pseudo-labels; crossover claim

label: deployment_threshold_vs_ranking_metrics

label: taxonomy_convention_artifacts
shared_hypothesis: Measured cross-domain/cross-dataset gaps are partly label-taxonomy and annotation-convention artifacts, quantifiable by small relabeling experiments.

label: synthetic_scaling_plateau_prediction
shared_hypothesis: The plateau of synthetic-data scaling is predictable in advance from generator-side or probe-side diversity measurements, before training full downstream models.

label: distribution_metrics_blind_to_task_value

members.one_line: Task utility is a third axis of the perception-distortion tradeoff that is non-monotonic in both: segmentation utility peaks at interior points no image metric identifies.

label: cfg_hidden_operating_knob
shared_hypothesis: Classifier-free-guidance scale is an unreported first-order operating knob: it monotonically trades memorization/precision against diversity/recall in downstream use, making unspecified-guidance comparisons meaningless.

label: rig_geometry_dominant_axis
shared_hypothesis: Camera rig geometry (pose, extrinsics) is the quietly dominant sim-to-real axis for mounted-camera domains; geometric resampling beats appearance-level adaptation, and randomizing it when deployment holds it fixed backfires.

label: label_view_mismatch
shared_hypothesis: Labels are drawn on views (enhanced, windowed, normalized) that differ from model inputs, so models chase structure that exists only in the annotation view; the bias is systematic and partly recoverable.

label: human_machine_preference_divergence
shared_hypothesis: Human perceptual preference and machine/metric utility systematically diverge: raters prefer outputs that score worse for machines, and the divergence has identifiable structure.

members.note: humans vs mIoU on segmentation quality; same divergence for masks

members.note: preference reverses with viewing zoom; protocol-validity law

label: hallucination_detection_signals
shared_hypothesis: Fabricated content in generative restoration is detectable from generator-internal signals (seed instability, internal features), but the detectors have identifiable failure conditions.

members.one_line: Hallucinated structures in generative restoration are unstable across sampler seeds while genuinely recovered structures are stable, enabling a training-free hallucination detector.
members.note: seed-instability separates fabricated from recovered structure

members.one_line: The internal features of a generative restorer identify which output pixels it invented, better than any image-space detector applied to its output.

members.one_line: Deterministic samplers do not reduce restoration hallucination; they make it reproducible, defeating ensemble-based detection while preserving the error.
members.note: TENSION/dependency: deterministic samplers make hallucination reproducible, defeating seed-ensemble detection

members.one_line: No-reference image quality metrics reward hallucination: adding fabricated detail raises NR-IQA scores even when fidelity to the true scene decreases.
members.note: NR-IQA rewards hallucination; metric complicity

members.one_line: No-reference IQA models have a structural blind spot for generative-restoration artifacts because they were trained on degradation artifacts, making them least reliable exactly where restoration pipelines need them.
members.note: NR-IQA structurally blind to generative artifacts; same metric-failure claim as w14w2b-018, mechanism form

label: nms_density_prior
shared_hypothesis: NMS and suppression stages encode hidden dataset-density priors and destroy recoverable information; much crowded-scene failure lives in suppression, not the network.

members.one_line: The optimal NMS IoU threshold is a hidden scene-density prior, and a per-image threshold predicted from a cheap pre-NMS density estimate recovers crowd recall without retraining
members.note: threshold as density prior; per-image adaptive fix

members.one_line: Soft-NMS gains are a dataset-density artifact: the soft-vs-hard ranking flips as a function of occlusion statistics, so the community's default choice encodes COCO's density
members.note: soft-vs-hard ranking flips with density statistics; same density-prior claim via method comparison

members.one_line: In crowded scenes most recall is lost inside the suppression stage, not the network: pre-NMS oracle recall stays high while post-NMS recall collapses
members.note: pre/post-NMS oracle recall localizes crowd failure to suppression

members.one_line: Detector-based counting saturates predictably in dense scenes, and the undercount is recoverable from pre-NMS score mass: a hybrid detector-regressor readout corrects counts without any new training
members.note: pre-NMS score mass recovers counts; application of the same recoverable-information claim

members.one_line: Score-ordered NMS keeps the most confident box, not the best-localized one, and the kept-vs-best localization gap is a measurable, correctable bias
members.note: score-ordered NMS keeps confident not best-localized box; selection-bias law

members.one_line: Crowd-region labels teach detectors to ignore dense clusters wholesale: recall inside iscrowd-style regions collapses even for clearly separable instances, and the suppression transfers to unlabeled crowd-like textures
members.note: iscrowd-region labels teach wholesale cluster suppression; training-data cause of crowd blindness

label: size_structured_calibration
shared_hypothesis: Detector/dense miscalibration is structured by object size and loss family rather than being a global temperature problem; size- and component-conditional recalibration fixes what global scaling cannot.

members.note: loss family determines calibration-curve signature

label: multilingual_query_asymmetry
shared_hypothesis: Multilingual queries expose text-encoder asymmetries in dense grounding: same-concept queries in different languages yield systematically different localizations.

label: finetuning_forgetting_frequency_order
shared_hypothesis: Fine-tuning erodes pretrained open-vocabulary/boundary knowledge in a predictable order (rare/abstract first, boundary-precision first), and the erosion is measurable mid-training.

label: grounding_bottleneck_location
shared_hypothesis: Where dense grounding fails architecturally: the vision encoder, the fusion stage, or the language side; members disagree on the locus, which is the decisive experiment.

label: prompt_template_fragility

label: lidar_sensor_physics
shared_hypothesis: The LiDAR sim-to-real gap is sensor-physics-structured (ray drop, intensity, beam divergence, timing), and physics-matched simulation or geometric resampling beats appearance-level adaptation; members disagree on whether to model or drop intensity.

members.note: TENSION: dropping the intensity channel improves transfer (avoid wrong reflectance model)

members.note: beam-pattern shift is a resampling problem, not adaptation

members.one_line: Missing rolling-shutter motion distortion in LiDAR simulation causes a specific real-world failure on fast crossing objects, and adding per-point timestamp skew to sim data fixes exactly that failure

label: lexical_vagueness_uncalibrated

members.one_line: Paraphrase disagreement is the best free uncertainty signal for dense outputs: variance across reworded queries predicts mask error better than confidence
members.note: paraphrase disagreement as free uncertainty signal; constructive use of the same language-conditioned uncertainty

label: ssl_vs_supervised_transfer
shared_hypothesis: What SSL-vs-supervised pretraining differences survive fine-tuning for localization tasks: members disagree whether the advantage vanishes or persists as complementary failure profiles.

label: A_renderer_fingerprints
