shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_A ideas under worker cluster 'lidar_driving_shift'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: Adverse-weather LiDAR shift is governed by the spatial clustering of particle returns, not their rate: simulations matching only drop/return rates fail, matching cluster statistics transfers

Cross-city and cross-country driving shifts are hierarchically different: cross-city is texture-level (adapting input statistics suffices), cross-country adds layout-grammar shift (requiring context relearning)
Traffic-agent behavior models in simulators leave layout signatures that segmentation models absorb: sim-trained models fail on real-but-implausible-in-sim configurations at predictable locations
Map-conditioned synthetic scene generation transfers better than free generation because layout comes from reality: the transferable component of driving scenes is the map, not the pixels
Night-driving domain shift is a mixture of two sub-domains (artificially lit vs unlit), and adapting to their mixture fails where per-sub-domain adaptation succeeds

label: A_vertical_domains
shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_A ideas under worker cluster 'vertical_domains'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: Underwater domain shift is parameterized by physical water type and range: attenuation-model-based augmentation (Jerlov-style parameter sweeps) beats learned style transfer for cross-water segmentation transfer

Generative models cannot synthesize useful industrial defect training data because defects are tail events: procedural physics-based defect models beat learned generators at matched effort, and the gap grows with defect rarity
Farm-to-farm shift in weed/crop segmentation is dominated by soil-background statistics, not plant appearance: background-swap synthetic data closes cross-farm gaps at near-zero generation cost
Greenhouse-to-field transfer is primarily an illumination-spectrum shift correctable by per-channel input renormalization, not a structural domain gap requiring retraining

Sim-to-real for fruit segmentation fails on occlusion statistics of foliage, not fruit appearance: procedural plant models with measured leaf-angle distributions beat photorealistic generative fruit imagery
Specular highlights on wet and polished industrial surfaces are the dominant unmodeled shift axis in factory deployments, and highlight-structure randomization beats global photometric randomization

Biofouling on fixed underwater cameras is a canonical slow distribution shift: performance decays along a measurable fouling trajectory and is recoverable by input-side compensation without retraining

Conveyor-belt wear is a slow domain drift with a knowable direction: pre-aging belt textures in training data ('drift-direction augmentation') inoculates food-processing segmentation against months of future drift
Cross-farm livestock segmentation shift is dominated by coat-pattern distribution differences between herds, and breed-conditioned synthetic coat randomization predicts and closes cross-farm gaps
Construction-site segmentation violates the stationary-domain assumption by design (the scene's own evolution is the shift), and time-conditioned training beats domain-adaptation framings

label: A_shift_measurement_science
shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_A ideas under worker cluster 'shift_measurement_science'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: Aggregate domain-shift metrics mislead because segmentation transfer is bottlenecked by the worst-shifted frequent class: a max-over-classes metric predicts transfer better than any mean
Shift metrics computed in task-trained feature spaces predict transfer better than metrics in general-purpose self-supervised spaces, and the difference grows with task specificity
Label-shift/covariate-shift decomposition is ill-posed at pixel level but well-posed at region level, and region-level decomposition predicts which adaptation method family will work
An 'augmentation compass': measuring target-domain distance separately along each augmentation axis predicts which augmentations will help, replacing trial-and-error augmentation search
Fifty labeled target images rank adaptation methods as reliably as full test sets, implying label-free shift estimation is over-invested relative to micro-labeling
Boundary F-score degrades before region IoU under gradually increasing shift, making boundary metrics an early-warning channel for deployment drift monitoring

Ensemble disagreement predicts transfer gap only when members differ in data ordering and augmentation draws, not just initialization seeds: diversity type, not diversity amount, drives shift detection

Entropy-reducing shifts (fog, blur, smoke) degrade segmentation gracefully while entropy-adding shifts (clutter, novel textures) degrade catastrophically, and an input entropy-delta statistic separates the regimes in advance
Cross-domain miscalibration of a segmentation model is predictable from its source-domain augmentation sensitivity, requiring no target data at all

label: A_adaptation_training_dynamics
shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_A ideas under worker cluster 'adaptation_training_dynamics'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: There is a critical period for domain diversity: synthetic-domain variety introduced late in training fails to confer robustness that the same variety introduced early provides
Batch composition (mixed synth-real batches vs alternating pure batches) changes normalization statistics enough to explain a chunk of reported adaptation gains, a confound in mixed-data experiments

Re-estimating only normalization statistics on the target domain recovers a large fraction of gains claimed by complex adaptation methods, and should be the mandatory null model for sim-to-real papers
Self-training on target pseudo-labels works mainly by re-fitting class decision thresholds, not by feature learning: a logit-adjustment-only control reproduces most of its gain
Domain-adversarial training's benefit is mostly generic regularization from gradient noise, not domain invariance: a matched-noise control without any domain discriminator reproduces the gains
Synthetic-data pretraining selects flatter loss-basins: robustness gains attributed to synthetic content partly reflect optimization geometry, testable by sharpness-matched controls
Low-realism-first curricula work through shape-bias induction: the ordering benefit exists only when early data has exaggerated shape cues, testable by cue-conflict evaluation
Interleaved sim-real cycling beats single-pass sim-then-real at equal compute: domain rehearsal prevents each domain's gains from overwriting the other's

Forgetting under domain shift is layer-heterogeneous: weight-consolidation penalties help backbones but actively hurt decoder heads, so uniform continual-learning regularization is miscalibrated for segmentation
Test-time adaptation amplifies synthetic-training biases: entropy minimization on real streams pushes synthetic-pretrained models toward their generator's systematic errors, a compounding interaction

label: A_synthetic_data_harms
shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_A ideas under worker cluster 'synthetic_data_harms'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: Harmful synthetic training samples are identifiable before training by gradient conflict against a small real anchor set, and pruning them beats training on everything
Synthetic data hurts exactly the classes it over-represents relative to the target label marginal: silent prior mismatch is a necessary-condition failure that class-frequency matching fixes for free
High-realism synthetic data can hurt more than low-realism data: near-domain errors are absorbed as facts while far-domain errors are discounted as noise (an uncanny-valley effect for training data)

Synthetic corpora have a 'poison tail': a small fraction of physically inconsistent images (impossible shadows, floating objects) causes disproportionate generalization damage, and physics-lint filters recover it
Synthetic-data harm is model-size-dependent with a sign flip: small models gain from the same corpus that hurts large models, because capacity determines whether generator quirks are fit

Mask-conditioned generation shrinks shape diversity: segmenters trained on generated pairs predict systematically smoother, more prototypical shapes, measurable as shape-distribution contraction on real data
Synthetic-trained models hallucinate structures resembling their generator's texture priors on real images, and the hallucinations are traceable by nearest-neighbor retrieval into the training corpus
Most synthetic-data harm is a late-layer phenomenon: dropping synthetic data for the last training epochs (real-only cool-down) retains the benefits and sheds the harms

label: A_domain_randomization_science
shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_A ideas under worker cluster 'domain_randomization_science'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: Domain randomization confers only a small subset of the invariances it nominally randomizes, and post-hoc invariance probing predicts its diminishing returns before scaling it up
DR axes are sub-additive because early layers absorb multiple randomizations with shared invariance machinery: texture and lighting randomization together yield less than the sum of their solo gains
Randomization ranges should match the target-domain variance, not maximize width: over-randomization measurably reduces feature specificity and caps transfer ('invariance overdraft')
Physically co-varying randomization (parameters sampled with realistic correlations) beats independent-axis randomization at matched sample count, because independence generates off-manifold worlds
DR's gains are largely predictable from gradient variance across randomized copies of the same scene, revealing it as a variance-reduction technique measurable before full training

The correct unit of randomization is the scene, not the image: within-scene appearance randomization (same layout, many appearances) teaches layout-invariant features faster than across-scene randomization
Curriculum DR (narrow-to-wide randomization ranges) avoids the early-training underfitting that wide-from-start DR causes, reaching better transfer at equal budget
A large share of DR's transfer benefit is reproducible by test-time augmentation ensembling on a non-randomized model, identifying which randomization axes truly need training-time exposure
Adversarially chosen randomization parameters (worst-case rendering per scene, selected by current-model failure) matches uniform DR's transfer with an order of magnitude fewer rendered images

label: A_shift_theory_taxonomy
shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_A ideas under worker cluster 'shift_theory_taxonomy'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: Segmentation domain shift factorizes into sensor, appearance, geometry, and layout tiers with a strict transfer-difficulty ordering, testable by constructing single-tier shifts

Shift effects compose predictably: performance under combined shifts is a simple function (approximately multiplicative in survival terms) of single-shift performances, enabling a 'shift algebra' for deployment forecasting
Class-agnostic boundary representations transfer across domains far better than class representations: boundary-first pretraining is a domain-generalization strategy, not just an architectural choice
Domain gap grows superlinearly with label-space granularity: fine-grained taxonomies amplify shift damage, making coarse-to-fine adaptation a principled (not just convenient) strategy
The domain-pair abstraction is wrong for deployment: shift arrives as ordered trajectories, and method rankings from pairwise benchmarks invert under trajectory evaluation
Per-class texture-vs-shape cue reliance measured on the source domain predicts per-class sim-to-real transfer without any target labels: a cue-reliance audit as a transfer forecast
ImageNet-style pretraining helps domain adaptation mostly through texture-statistics coverage, not semantics: label-free texture-corpus pretraining matches it for segmentation transfer
Sim-to-real transfer is bottlenecked by the decoder, not the encoder: frozen synthetic-trained encoders with real-data-tuned decoders recover most of the gap, localizing where domain knowledge lives

label: B_restoration_segmentation_coupling
shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_B ideas under worker cluster 'restoration_segmentation_coupling'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: Super-resolving images before segmentation improves mask plausibility while decreasing fidelity to the true scene, because predicted boundaries snap to hallucinated edges.
MMSE-optimal denoising selectively erases low-contrast thin structures, so denoising can raise PSNR while lowering thin-class segmentation recall.
Restoration models pretrained on natural images impose natural-scene priors that misinterpret domain-specific structures as artifacts and remove them.
Jointly trained restoration-plus-segmentation systems pass segmentation hints through the restored image as imperceptible signals rather than genuinely improving image quality.
Restoration-induced boundary shifts are directional (systematic erosion or dilation per structure type), not zero-mean noise, so they bias measurements rather than adding variance.
Segmentation networks are far more robust to texture-destroying degradations than to contour-degrading ones, inverting the texture-bias narrative imported from classification.
Restoration and segmentation models share the same learned natural-image prior, so their errors are correlated and cascade ensembling yields far less than independence predicts.
The residual uncertainty of a restoration model predicts where a downstream segmenter will fail better than the segmenter's own confidence does.
Downstream segmentation accuracy versus SR upscaling factor is non-monotonic, peaking below the native resolution at the onset of hallucination.
Motion deblurring collapses the exposure interval to an arbitrary instant, so segmenting deblurred frames localizes moving objects at a biased time point.

label: B_hallucination_fabrication
shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_B ideas under worker cluster 'hallucination_fabrication'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: Generative restoration replaces rare structures with frequent lookalikes (mode substitution), silently collapsing rare-class recall in downstream segmentation.
Generative restoration completes broken contours using amodal-completion priors, injecting false connectivity into vessel, crack, and boundary topology.
Restoration hallucination is frequency-anisotropic: fabricated fine texture is spatially well-placed while mid-frequency structure is misplaced, concentrating downstream errors at object scale.
SR models snap ambiguous glyph-like regions to valid-looking characters, producing confidently wrong text and markings in restored images and their segmentations.
Fabrication rate in generative restoration varies systematically with image position, inheriting the spatial composition bias of the generator's training data.
Super-resolution amplifies adversarial perturbations: imperceptible LR-space attacks can steer restored content and flip downstream segmentation at will.
Chained restoration operations compound fabrication superlinearly, and pipeline order changes what gets invented more than parameter settings do.

label: B_degradation_physics
shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_B ideas under worker cluster 'degradation_physics'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: The synthetic-to-real robustness gap in degraded-image segmentation is largely noise-model mis-specification with a predictable failure direction, not an amorphous domain gap.
Segmentation models exploit demosaicing correlations as features, so RAW-trained and RGB-trained models generalize differently under resampling and novel sensors.
Photon noise is informative, not just corruptive: noise variance encodes luminance, and segmentation networks measurably use it, which denoising removes.
Segmentation accuracy under increasing degradation collapses in class-specific phase transitions predictable from each class's spatial-frequency signature.
Robust segmentation networks implicitly perform blind blur-kernel estimation: the point-spread function is decodable from their features, explaining and bounding their deblurring-free robustness.
The anti-aliasing kernel used when datasets are resized is an unreported hyperparameter that measurably re-ranks segmentation methods on public benchmarks.
Dehazing systematically relocates the boundary between distant objects and sky or background, acting as a learned horizon prior rather than a neutral contrast restorer.
Global exposure and gamma changes act on segmentation like class-prior shifts, changing per-class recall in lawful, predictable directions rather than adding uniform noise.

label: B_diffusion_priors_features
shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_B ideas under worker cluster 'diffusion_priors_features'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: Diffusion-model features encode boundary ownership (which object an edge belongs to) more explicitly than discriminative pretraining features.
The best diffusion timestep for segmentation features depends on object size, so any single-timestep feature extraction is provably suboptimal.
The geometry of the learned score field performs zero-shot segmentation: at moderate noise, score vectors point from boundaries toward region interiors.
Pixels that are unstable under diffusion inversion and regeneration mark object boundaries, giving an unsupervised boundary detector from any pretrained diffusion model.
Cross-attention maps in text-to-image diffusion systematically under-segment objects, attending to discriminative parts, with the deficit growing with object articulation.
Generative (diffusion-likelihood) and discriminative segmentation errors overlap precisely on ambiguous boundary pixels, so their combination fails where combination is most needed.

Diffusion features sweep from texture-dominant to shape-dominant along the noise axis, and a model's transfer quality to a segmentation domain is predictable from where that domain needs to sit on the spectrum.
Fine-tuning diffusion models for generation quality destroys their segmentation-relevant features faster than generation metrics degrade, decoupling the two capabilities.
Diffusion-feature segmenters fail predictably in regions the generator cannot generate well: generability maps forecast failure geography before any labels exist.
Emergent correspondence in diffusion features is instance-blind: on scenes with repeated objects it matches category, not instance, corrupting correspondence-based segmentation propagation.
Text conditioning is a hidden test-time variable in diffusion-feature segmentation: changing an ostensibly irrelevant prompt flips downstream mask decisions.
Generative priors impose a closed vocabulary through the back door: objects the generator cannot synthesize get feature-assimilated to their nearest generable category.
Averaging diffusion features across timesteps helps segmentation because different timesteps segment different semantic granularities, not because averaging reduces noise.

label: B_diffusion_segmentation_models
shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_B ideas under worker cluster 'diffusion_segmentation_models'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: Diffusion segmentation models sample plausible masks, not posterior samples: their mask distribution is measurably under-dispersed relative to annotator distributions.
The celebrated diversity of diffusion segmentation is boundary jitter, not hypothesis-level diversity: samples rarely differ in topology or structure the way annotators do.
The argmax decoding step at the end of mask diffusion destroys the learned distribution, and decoding choice changes reported accuracy more than most architectural contributions.
The denoising trajectory of mask diffusion reveals a consistent coarse-to-fine part hierarchy, providing an unsupervised scene-parsing signal in the order structures emerge.
Most trained mask-diffusion models are secretly deterministic: their output barely depends on the noise input, making the diffusion machinery dead weight at inference.
More denoising steps can make segmentation masks worse: mask quality is non-monotonic in sampling steps because later steps impose the mask prior over image evidence.
The standard denoising objective mis-weights segmentation errors by object area, predictably sacrificing small objects relative to discriminative training at matched capacity.
Image-conditioned mask diffusion decides mask layout from the dataset prior early in the trajectory, consulting the image mainly for late refinement: conditioning arrives too late.
Inpainting-style local mask editing with diffusion models is nonlocal: correcting one region measurably changes distant, untouched regions of the mask.
Continuous relaxation of categorical masks in diffusion biases boundary placement systematically compared to discrete diffusion, an unexamined determinant of boundary metrics.
Sample-variance maps from diffusion segmentation at practical sample counts measure sampler noise, not ambiguity: the variance map barely changes when ambiguity does.
Self-conditioning in mask diffusion causes error lock-in: mistakes made early in the trajectory persist to the final mask instead of being iteratively refined away.
Denoising-pretrained and inpainting-pretrained models transfer to segmentation with dissociable failure modes: boundary-sharpening false positives versus region-completion false negatives.

label: B_perception_distortion_downstream
shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_B ideas under worker cluster 'perception_distortion_downstream'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: The utility-optimal restoration depends on which segmentation metric will be used: boundary-metric consumers need different restorations than region-metric consumers.
Average distortion metrics hide class-conditional utility loss: restoration that improves overall image quality degrades minority-class segmentation, and the curves cross.
Restoration helps segmentation only below an input-quality threshold and strictly hurts above it, and the community averages across regimes into a meaningless net effect.
Task-aware restoration trained with segmentation losses learns to paint faint class-boundary contours into images rather than restoring them, so gains do not transfer to other segmenters.

LPIPS-optimized restoration preferentially preserves classification-relevant information because LPIPS is built on classification features, measurably sacrificing the spatial precision dense tasks need.
Human-optimized codecs misallocate bits against segmentation needs in a measurable, spatially structured way: utility-per-bit concentrates at boundaries that codecs deprioritize.

label: B_synthetic_loops_contamination
shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_B ideas under worker cluster 'synthetic_loops_contamination'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: Gains from diffusion-generated training data are partly artifact shortcuts: models key on generator fingerprints co-occurring with clean synthetic labels, and gains shrink when fingerprints are removed.
Co-generated image-mask training pairs align too perfectly: models trained on them acquire unrealistic boundary-precision expectations that degrade performance on human-annotated reality.
Copy-paste and diffusion-inpainting augmentation teach opposite lessons: one builds boundary-artifact robustness, the other builds context-object binding that fails under context shift.

label: B_microscopy_wsi
shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_B ideas under worker cluster 'microscopy_wsi'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: Self-supervised microscopy denoisers delete dim puncta by design, biasing count-based biology downward in proportion to structure sparsity.
Gigapixel WSI stitching seams create phantom boundaries that segmentation models learn to avoid, and benchmark scores are inflated because annotations systematically exclude seam regions.
A large share of hard cases in pathology segmentation benchmarks are focus artifacts, not difficult biology: local focus score predicts error better than any semantic variable.
Computational super-resolution microscopy reconstructions impose continuity priors that fabricate filament connections, making a fraction of downstream cytoskeleton topology algorithmic artifact.
Scanner-side JPEG2000 compression degrades diagnostic chromatin texture before stromal texture, making nuclei-subtype segmentation compression-fragile in a predictable order.
Pathology models entangle two size signals: microns-per-pixel metadata errors reveal whether models read absolute cell size as diagnostic signal or as scanner shortcut.
Natural-image diffusion priors impose reflected-light shading physics on transmitted-light microscopy, producing plausible-but-wrong intensity structure that biases confluence and density estimates.
Patch-based WSI segmentation has a measurable context ceiling: pathologists' region boundaries depend on gigapixel-scale architecture that no patch-level model can access.
Denoising-enabled low-light live-cell imaging changes the biology it measures: residual restoration bias correlates with motion, distorting motility statistics.
Learned axial super-resolution in volumetric microscopy fabricates 3D morphology: isotropy-restored volumes bias shape metrics like sphericity in a consistent, quantifiable direction.
Virtual staining is segmentation laundering: evaluating segmentation on virtually stained images double-counts the staining model's prior and reports information the input never contained.
WSI foundation-model embeddings encode scanner identity more strongly than tissue class at shallow depths, and restoration-style harmonization removes diagnostic signal along with the scanner signal.

label: B_video_streaming
shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_B ideas under worker cluster 'video_streaming'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: Temporal-consistency training installs persistence bias: consistency-optimized video segmenters are systematically late and inaccurate on object state changes.
Frame interpolation fabricates linear motion, so segmentation and tracking on interpolated video infer wrong occlusion order at object crossings.
Video diffusion restoration imposes object permanence beyond evidence: departed objects get regenerated, and downstream trackers report phantom re-identifications.
Segmentation models silently correct rolling-shutter distortions of fast-moving objects toward canonical shapes, corrupting downstream geometry instead of reporting the distortion.
Auto-exposure transients cause time-locked segmentation dropouts that shuffled-frame evaluation cannot detect, making deployed streaming accuracy lower than benchmarked accuracy.
Duplicate frames and variable frame rates in web training video teach a spurious zero-motion prior: slow-moving objects are under-segmented relative to static ones of identical appearance.
Event cameras contribute boundary re-localization rather than object discovery to segmentation: fusion gains decompose almost entirely into boundary-metric improvements.

label: B_evaluation_science
shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_B ideas under worker cluster 'evaluation_science'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: Evaluating restored-image segmentation against clean-image ground truth credits hallucination: an evidence-limited ground-truth protocol flips method rankings.
Boundary metrics are not resolution-invariant: evaluating the same predictions at different resolutions re-ranks methods, and SR-and-restoration papers implicitly exploit favorable evaluation scales.
Generalized energy distance rewards degenerate diversity: adding structured noise samples improves GED scores for multi-sample segmentation without adding any valid interpretation.
Reported diffusion-segmentation advantages shrink or vanish under compute-matched comparison: multi-step sampling budgets, given to discriminative ensembles, close most published gaps.

label: C_anti_scaling_dense
shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_C ideas under worker cluster 'anti_scaling_dense'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: Backbone-scaling gains in semantic segmentation are largely effective-resolution artifacts, not representation gains.
Boundary quality anti-scales: bigger segmentation models get relatively worse at boundaries as they get better at regions.
Web-scale pretraining makes long-tail segmentation classes worse, not better, past a data threshold.
Claimed emergent zero-shot segmentation abilities are thresholded-metric artifacts, not capability jumps.
Per-domain small specialists beat one large generalist segmenter at equal total inference cost.
Scaling same-protocol annotation converges to protocol bias, not to ground truth.
Over-pretraining exists: dense transfer peaks and then degrades as SSL pretraining runs longer.
Compute-optimal scaling recipes imported from language mispredict segmentation because resolution is the missing third axis.
Diverse small-model ensembles beat scale-matched single large segmenters out of distribution, reversing the in-distribution verdict.

label: C_nonreplication_method_families
shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_C ideas under worker cluster 'nonreplication_method_families'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: Boundary-aware loss functions stop beating plain cross-entropy once the baseline gets the same tuning budget.
Mask-classification decoder heads owe most of their reported edge over per-pixel heads to training recipes, not architecture.
Test-time augmentation for segmentation loses to a single higher-resolution pass at matched inference FLOPs.
Deep supervision and auxiliary segmentation heads are an optimizer-era relic with near-zero modern effect.
CRF and refinement post-processing now hurts as often as it helps, with a predictable flip point in backbone quality.
Plug-and-play attention modules for segmentation add seed-level noise, not signal, once parameters are matched.
Curriculum ordering of training images does not replicate for segmentation once the LR schedule is re-tuned per arm.
Hard-example mining and class-rebalancing exploit the same slack; combined they add nothing and OHEM alone loses to plain resampling.
Frequency-domain segmentation modules exploit compression-pipeline artifacts, and their gains vanish on recompression-controlled data.
Pixel-contrastive pretraining does not beat masked-image-modeling for segmentation once pretraining compute is matched.
Domain-generalization methods for segmentation stop working once the baseline uses modern strong augmentation.

label: C_pretraining_transfer_myths
shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_C ideas under worker cluster 'pretraining_transfer_myths'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: The ImageNet-pretraining crossover for segmentation happens at far smaller dataset sizes than practitioners assume.
Geometry pretraining negatively transfers to semantic boundaries where depth edges and semantic edges disagree.
Intermediate-task segmentation transfer is governed by annotation-protocol match, not semantic similarity.
Video pretraining adds nothing for still-image segmentation once frame counts are matched to image pretraining.
Multi-dataset universal segmentation training hides per-dataset regressions caused by taxonomy conflicts.
Model merging and task arithmetic break down for dense prediction: segmentation task vectors do not compose.

label: C_adversarial_robustness_contrarian
shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_C ideas under worker cluster 'adversarial_robustness_contrarian'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: Lp-adversarial training for segmentation buys almost no protection against physically realizable attacks.
Published robust-segmentation numbers are inflated by gradient masking; dense-aware adaptive attacks will halve them.
Certified segmentation robustness certifies the easy pixels: interiors get certificates, boundaries never do.
Black-box transferability of segmentation attacks is far weaker than the classification-derived threat narrative claims.
The robustness-accuracy tradeoff in segmentation is an artifact of importing classification epsilon budgets.
Single-frame adversarial patch alarm is overstated: trivial temporal aggregation collapses patch attack success on video segmentation.
Strong data augmentation delivers most of adversarial training's robustness for segmentation at a fraction of the cost.
Dense supervision is an implicit adversarial regularizer: segmenters are naturally harder to fully break than classifiers on the same backbone.
Adversarial-input detectors ported to segmentation fail against region-targeted attacks that leave global statistics untouched.
Robustness is dataset-idiosyncratic: adversarially robust segmentation backbones do not stay robust after fine-tuning elsewhere.
Promptable segmentation robustness numbers are inflated because evaluations attack per-prompt instead of prompt-agnostically.

label: C_fairness_bias_contrarian
shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_C ideas under worker cluster 'fairness_bias_contrarian'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: Skin-tone segmentation gaps are mostly photometric, not representational: luminance-matched evaluation erases the majority of the gap.
Group-balancing training data fails to close segmentation gaps because the gaps live in annotation quality, not sample counts.
Classification-born fairness interventions equalize image-level metrics while worsening boundary-level disparities in dense prediction.
Geographic segmentation gaps are scene-composition effects, not appearance effects: models fail on unfamiliar layouts, not unfamiliar objects.
Reported demographic gaps in human parsing can flip sign under alternative reasonable annotation conventions.
Worst-group-optimizing training makes the worst group worse on clean re-annotated ground truth by overfitting its label noise.
Clothing contrast dwarfs demographic attributes as the driver of pedestrian segmentation failure, but only demographics get measured.
Face-blurring training data costs segmentation models almost nothing, contradicting the raw-data-retention argument.
Demographic gaps in medical segmentation are mostly scanner and site confounds, not patient-attribute effects.
Generative rebalancing backfires: synthetic minority-group images degrade minority-group segmentation because generators are worse for those groups.
Test-set composition moves measured group gaps more than model interventions do: the bias is in the benchmark, not the model.

label: C_data_quantity_myths
shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_C ideas under worker cluster 'data_quantity_myths'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: Fixing existing label errors beats collecting new images per annotation-hour, up to surprisingly large dataset sizes.
Web-scale pretraining corpora are effectively far smaller than advertised: near-duplicate structure makes dense-transfer gains track deduplicated size, not raw size.
Classification-derived dataset-pruning scores pick the wrong images for segmentation; dense-specific pruning keeps quality at much higher pruning rates.
Annotation granularity beats image count: fewer images with part-level masks outperform many images with coarse masks at equal annotation time.
At equal annotation cost, sparse point and scribble supervision matches dense masks, making dense mask labeling economically irrational for many projects.
Class-balanced training is not the optimum for segmentation: instance-count balancing beats pixel balancing, and both lose to loss-adaptive sampling.
Past a modest scale, hard negatives (target-free images) buy more deployed reliability than additional positives, but datasets keep growing positives.
Random train/val splits on session-structured datasets leak near-duplicates and inflate segmentation scores; session-stratified splits reorder published methods.
Verify-and-correct beats from-scratch human annotation on quality, not just cost: the gold-standard hierarchy is backwards.
Tail-class segmentation is bottlenecked by head-class boundary quality, not tail sample counts: fixing head labels helps the tail more than adding tail data.

label: C_augmentation_myths
shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_C ideas under worker cluster 'augmentation_myths'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: Copy-paste and CutMix buy region accuracy while corrupting boundary learning: models learn that hard straight edges are class boundaries.
Multi-scale inference is redundant once crop-scale augmentation is tuned: the machinery survives on under-tuned training baselines.
Color jitter destroys the signal for color-defined classes, and models pass benchmarks anyway by exploiting shape shortcuts that fail in deployment.
Consistency-regularization training is inference-time ensembling in disguise: its gain equals averaging two augmented predictions of the baseline.
Augmentation strength should shrink with dataset scale, and past a size threshold strong augmentation becomes net harmful in-domain.
Elastic deformation, the canonical medical augmentation, adds nothing on modern architectures: its benefit was a capacity-era artifact.
Test-time augmentation increases per-image regressions even while raising the mean: it is not the safe free accuracy it is sold as.
Learned augmentation policies transferred from classification search underperform hand-set simple augmentation for segmentation.

label: C_architecture_narrative_reversals
shared_hypothesis: Theme group (not duplicates): remaining worker_C ideas under worker cluster 'architecture_narrative_reversals'; grouped for consolidator navigation only.

members.one_line: The transformers-beat-CNNs verdict for segmentation is a training-recipe artifact, not an architectural fact.
U-Net skip connections mainly transport boundary detail, not semantics: replacing skip content with edge maps preserves most performance.
Dilated convolutions are a low-resolution-era workaround that modern pipelines no longer need.
Global attention is wasted on most pixels: windowed attention with zero cross-window communication matches global models on all but a small class subset.
Parameter allocation in segmentation models is backwards: past a modest backbone size, decoder capacity and decoder resolution dominate marginal gains.
Object-query architectures memorize dataset shape priors and lose to per-pixel heads on shape-out-of-distribution instances.
Positional embeddings let segmenters memorize benchmark layout statistics; part of reported progress is layout memorization, not perception.
Full-resolution inference is mostly wasted compute: half-resolution prediction with a learned edge-aware upsampler matches it.
Normalization-statistic choices move segmentation results more than the architectural contributions claimed in the same papers.
